subject: tourism
description: Tourism skill tree, FET Grades 10-12 (CAPS FET Tourism Grades 10-12). 9 CAPS topics: Tourism sectors; Map work & tour planning; Tourism attractions; Sustainable & responsible tourism; Domestic, regional & international tourism; Culture & heritage tourism; Foreign exchange; Communication & customer care; Marketing. Tiers = CAPS terms within a grade (T1-T4). Mastery = 60% of a 20-item pool (FET rule, no timer). ALL questions available — no prerequisites between skills, learner chooses any skill in any order. Input types: choice, true-false, cloze, sequence, image-match (existing) + sort-buckets, highlight-source, argument-builder, paragraph-template, source-comparison (tap-based mechanics, no free-text). Any question may carry an optional 'source' block (text extract, map, photo, brochure or statistics table with provenance). Items live in data/tourism-question-bank.json. v1.0: Grade 10 fully authored as proof (28 skills, ~560 items); Grades 11-12 pending head-of-ed review of this structure.

levels.title: Grade 10 — Tourism
levels.description: Foundations across eight of the nine CAPS topics (Foreign exchange begins in Grade 11). T1: tourism sectors — tourists, transport, accommodation, food & beverage, attractions, the industry structure, and payment. T2: map work & domestic tourism. T3: South African attractions, sustainable & responsible tourism, and marketing. T4: culture & heritage, communication & customer care. 28 atomic skills, all unlocked, learner-chosen order.

atomic_skills.title: Introduction to tourism
atomic_skills.description: What tourism is; the difference between inbound and outbound tourism; the concepts domestic, regional and international tourism; what a tourist is; why people travel; and tourists' needs, preferences and expectations.

error_signatures.description: Confuses inbound/outbound with domestic/international
error_signatures.example: Calls a South African holidaying in Cape Town an inbound tourist

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Anchor on the traveller's home country and direction of travel: inbound = into SA from abroad; outbound = SA residents going abroad; domestic = travel inside one's own country.

atomic_skills.title: Types of tourists & tourist profiles
atomic_skills.description: Recognising types of tourists (VFR, leisure, adventure, business, shopping, health, eco, cultural, religious, sport & recreation, education, special interest, incentive, backpacker/youth, gap year) and drawing up a tourist profile linking needs and preferences.

error_signatures.description: Matches the wrong tourist type to a motivation
error_signatures.example: Labels a person attending a trade fair an 'eco' tourist

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Identify the main PURPOSE of the trip first — that purpose names the tourist type (visiting family = VFR; nature with low impact = eco; reward trip paid by employer = incentive).

atomic_skills.title: Modes of transport
atomic_skills.description: Road, air, rail, water and extraordinary modes with examples; comparing them on comfort, cost, safety, carrying capacity, speed and reliability; advantages and disadvantages of each.

error_signatures.description: Misplaces a mode in the wrong category
error_signatures.example: Lists a tram under water transport

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Sort by the surface the vehicle moves on: road (car/bus/taxi), rail (train/tram), air (plane/helicopter), water (cruise/yacht), extraordinary (camel/balloon).

atomic_skills.title: Accommodation establishments — types, facilities & services
atomic_skills.description: Formal-service, guest, self-catering, caravan/camping and backpacker accommodation; the difference between a facility (what the tourist can use) and a service (what the establishment does for the tourist).

error_signatures.description: Confuses a facility with a service
error_signatures.example: Calls a 24-hour laundry a facility

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A facility is a THING the guest uses (pool, gym, gift shop). A service is an ACTION staff perform (laundry, guided walk, shuttle).

atomic_skills.title: The South African grading system
atomic_skills.description: The star grading system; the role of the Tourism Grading Council of South Africa (TGCSA); the benefits of grading for tourists and establishments; the procedure to be graded; logos displayed on grading.

error_signatures.description: Thinks grading is compulsory or set by the establishment itself
error_signatures.example: Says a hotel awards its own stars

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Grading in SA is VOLUNTARY and awarded by an independent body (TGCSA), not by the establishment. More stars = higher quality of facilities and service.

atomic_skills.title: Accommodation terminology & in-room technology
atomic_skills.description: Concepts and abbreviations used in accommodation (twin/double/family room, suite, en suite, per person sharing, fully inclusive, B&B, a la carte, pp/pps/pppn/pppd) and in-room technology for entertainment, information, safety, comfort, work and environmental responsibility.

error_signatures.description: Misreads an abbreviation
error_signatures.example: Reads pps as 'per person sharing per night'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Break the abbreviation into parts: pp = per person, pps = per person sharing, pppn = per person per night, pppd = per person per day.

atomic_skills.title: Food & beverage establishments
atomic_skills.description: Types of food and beverage establishments: full-service restaurants (fine-dining and family), coffee shops, fast-food/quick-service, pubs/bars, dessert/ice-cream stores, taverns/shebeens, street stalls and markets.

error_signatures.description: Confuses service style across establishment types
error_signatures.example: Describes a fast-food outlet as fine dining

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Match the establishment to its service style and speed: fine-dining = full table service; quick-service = fast, counter-based; coffee shop = light meals and drinks.

atomic_skills.title: The attraction sector
atomic_skills.description: Attraction subsectors (gaming, leisure, conservation, sport & recreation, events & conferences); man-made vs natural attractions; primary vs secondary attractions; activities offered; linking an attraction to the tourist type it appeals to.

error_signatures.description: Confuses primary and secondary attractions
error_signatures.example: Calls a museum visited on the side the primary reason for the trip

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: The PRIMARY attraction is the main reason for the trip; SECONDARY attractions are extras visited while there. Man-made is built by people; natural occurs in nature.

atomic_skills.title: Structure of the SA tourism industry
atomic_skills.description: Tourism as a partnership between the public sector (national/provincial/local government and parastatals), the private sector (product owners that profit from tourism) and local communities; the logo, function and service of key associations (TBCSA, TGCSA, FTTSA, SATSA, FEDHASA, ASATA).

error_signatures.description: Places a body in the wrong sector
error_signatures.example: Lists a private tour operator under the public sector

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Public sector = government and its agencies (funded by the state). Private sector = businesses that make a profit from tourism. Communities = the people living where tourism happens.

atomic_skills.title: Payment methods & technology in South Africa
atomic_skills.description: Payment methods and the technology behind them (internet payments, ATMs, cellphone payments, fixed and portable speed points, credit cards, debit cards, cheques); their advantages and disadvantages; choosing the most appropriate method for a situation.

error_signatures.description: Confuses credit and debit cards
error_signatures.example: Says a debit card lets you spend the bank's money on credit

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A debit card spends YOUR OWN money already in the account; a credit card borrows the bank's money to be repaid later.

atomic_skills.title: Map terminology & symbols
atomic_skills.description: Map concepts: scale, direction, distance indicators, legends, grid references, equator, hemispheres, poles, latitude, longitude, time zones, Universal Time Coordinate (UTC) and the International Date Line (IDL).

error_signatures.description: Confuses latitude and longitude
error_signatures.example: Says lines of longitude run east-west

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Latitude lines run across (like rungs of a ladder, measuring north-south position); longitude lines run top-to-bottom between the poles (measuring east-west position).

atomic_skills.title: Types of maps in a tourism context
atomic_skills.description: Road/street maps, political maps, physical maps, specialist maps (climate, airports, railways), tourist information maps, and electronic maps (GPS, Google Maps, Google Earth) — their uses and value in tourism.

error_signatures.description: Picks the wrong map for a task
error_signatures.example: Uses a political map to find mountain heights

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Match the map to the question: borders/capitals = political; landforms = physical; getting from A to B = road/GPS; attractions in an area = tourist information map.

atomic_skills.title: Locating features on a map of South Africa
atomic_skills.description: Locating South Africa's borders, provinces, capital cities, international airports, harbours, national highways, gateways, major mountains, rivers and dams on a colour map.

error_signatures.description: Misplaces a province or capital
error_signatures.example: Places Bloemfontein in the Western Cape

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Build a mental map from the coast inward: coastal provinces (WC, EC, KZN) ring the south and east; the interior holds Free State, Gauteng, North West, Mpumalanga, Limpopo and Northern Cape.

atomic_skills.title: Locating SADC, continents, oceans & tourism regions
atomic_skills.description: Locating South Africa and the SADC countries, the seven continents, three oceans, island groups and the major tourism regions (Far East, Middle East, UK, Europe, the Americas, Australasia) on a colour map of the world.

error_signatures.description: Confuses a continent with a tourism region
error_signatures.example: Lists 'Western Europe' as a continent

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: There are 7 continents (fixed) and 3 oceans; tourism regions are travel-industry groupings of countries within or across continents.

atomic_skills.title: Distance indicators & distance tables
atomic_skills.description: Using distance indicators on maps and distance tables to work out distances between towns and cities, and linking distance to travelling time (roughly 100 km per hour).

error_signatures.description: Reads the wrong cell of a distance table
error_signatures.example: Reads across the wrong row when both cities are listed

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Find one city on the top and the other down the side; the cell where the row and column meet is the distance. Divide km by 100 for an approximate drive in hours.

atomic_skills.title: Domestic tourism — concepts, benefits & Sho't Left
atomic_skills.description: The concept of domestic tourism; its benefits for South Africa's economy, people and environment; and the Sho't Left campaign that promotes travel within South Africa.

error_signatures.description: Confuses domestic tourism with inbound tourism
error_signatures.example: Says foreign visitors are domestic tourists

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Domestic tourism = residents travelling WITHIN their own country. Sho't Left encourages South Africans to take affordable local trips.

atomic_skills.title: Interpreting domestic tourism statistics
atomic_skills.description: Concepts of statistics and intra- vs inter-provincial travel; interpreting statistics on purpose of trips, most-visited provinces, length of stay, average expenditure and seasonality.

error_signatures.description: Confuses intra- and inter-provincial travel
error_signatures.example: Calls travel between Gauteng and KZN intra-provincial

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Intra- = WITHIN one province (intra = inside). Inter- = BETWEEN provinces. Read graph titles and axes before drawing a conclusion.

atomic_skills.title: Tourist attractions in the provinces of South Africa
atomic_skills.description: Key attractions in each of the nine provinces — their location (nearest city/town) and main focus — including World Heritage Sites such as the Cradle of Humankind, Robben Island, iSimangaliso and Mapungubwe.

error_signatures.description: Places an attraction in the wrong province
error_signatures.example: Locates Table Mountain in the Eastern Cape

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Anchor each attraction to its nearest major city, then to that city's province (Table Mountain - Cape Town - Western Cape).

atomic_skills.title: SANParks, transfrontier parks & private reserves
atomic_skills.description: What a national park is and why tourists visit; Kruger as the flagship; other national parks and their conservation focus; transfrontier parks and conservation areas; and luxury private game reserves (Shamwari, Madikwe, Phinda, Sabi Sabi).

error_signatures.description: Confuses a transfrontier park with a single-country park
error_signatures.example: Says Kgalagadi is entirely inside South Africa

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A transfrontier park crosses an international BORDER and is shared by two or more countries; a national park sits within one country.

atomic_skills.title: South African fauna, flora & botanical gardens
atomic_skills.description: Concepts of biodiversity, ecosystem, species, habitat, endangered, indigenous, alien, poaching and culling in a tourism context; national botanical gardens with Kirstenbosch as the flagship.

error_signatures.description: Confuses indigenous and alien species
error_signatures.example: Calls an introduced foreign plant indigenous

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Indigenous = naturally occurring in that place; alien = brought in from elsewhere. Endangered = at risk of dying out; extinct = already gone.

atomic_skills.title: Sustainable tourism — the three pillars
atomic_skills.description: What sustainability means in tourism; the need for sustainable practices; the three pillars (planet/environmental, people/social, profit/economic) and the impact of tourism businesses on each.

error_signatures.description: Assigns an impact to the wrong pillar
error_signatures.example: Files 'creates local jobs' under the environmental pillar

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Three Ps: Planet (environment), People (communities/society), Profit (economy). Ask which one an example most affects.

atomic_skills.title: Responsible tourism & good environmental practices
atomic_skills.description: Responsible tourist behaviour towards the environment and host communities; the negative impacts of tourism; rules for behaviour in nature; and good environmental practices (litter control, conserving energy and water) and their benefits.

error_signatures.description: Confuses sustainable tourism (the goal) with responsible tourism (the behaviour)
error_signatures.example: Uses the terms interchangeably with no distinction

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Sustainable tourism is the GOAL (lasting balance of planet/people/profit); responsible tourism is the BEHAVIOUR of tourists and businesses that helps reach it.

atomic_skills.title: Global warming & the tourism industry
atomic_skills.description: The concepts of global warming and carbon footprint; causes of global warming; consequences of climate change for tourism; and how establishments and tourists can reduce their carbon footprint.

error_signatures.description: Confuses carbon footprint with general litter/pollution
error_signatures.example: Says recycling paper directly lowers a carbon footprint more than reducing flights

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: A carbon footprint measures greenhouse gases released by an activity. The biggest tourism contributors are transport (especially flights) and energy use.

atomic_skills.title: Marketing of tourism products, services & sites
atomic_skills.description: Marketing concepts (market research, target market, market share, competitive edge, niche market); the purpose of marketing; the market-research process and the marketing mix (the five Ps: product, promotion, price, place, people).

error_signatures.description: Confuses target market with market share
error_signatures.example: Defines market share as the group a product is aimed at

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Target market = the GROUP you aim a product at. Market share = the PORTION of total sales a business holds. The five Ps are product, promotion, price, place, people.

atomic_skills.title: Culture & heritage — concepts and elements
atomic_skills.description: The concepts culture, heritage and cultural diversity; elements of culture (architecture, interiors, arts and crafts, cuisine, music and dance); and the importance of conserving heritage for future generations.

error_signatures.description: Confuses culture with heritage
error_signatures.example: Uses 'heritage' to mean only present-day customs

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Culture = a group's shared way of life NOW (food, music, dress). Heritage = what is INHERITED from the past and worth conserving for the future.

atomic_skills.title: Heritage sites in South Africa
atomic_skills.description: Cultural heritage sites (monuments, museums, historical buildings, graveyards) and natural heritage sites (mountains, waterfalls, caves); the difference between local, provincial and national heritage sites; and the heritage plaque that marks a national site.

error_signatures.description: Confuses cultural and natural heritage sites
error_signatures.example: Classifies a waterfall as a cultural heritage site

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Cultural heritage = made or shaped by PEOPLE (monuments, buildings). Natural heritage = formed by NATURE (mountains, caves, waterfalls).

atomic_skills.title: Communication & communication technology
atomic_skills.description: Equipment used to communicate in a tourism business (landlines, cellphones, fax, photocopiers, printers, computers with email, video- and teleconferencing) and their functions, advantages and disadvantages; verbal and written communication including email netiquette and tourism road/information signs.

error_signatures.description: Confuses verbal and written communication
error_signatures.example: Lists an email as verbal communication

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Verbal = SPOKEN (face-to-face, phone). Written = recorded in TEXT (email, SMS, memo, fax). Netiquette = good manners when communicating online.

atomic_skills.title: Service excellence
atomic_skills.description: The concepts service and service excellence; the importance and value of quality service for a tourism business; the advantages of excellent service for the business and the tourist; the consequences of poor service; and recommendations for improvement.

error_signatures.description: Sees service excellence as a cost rather than an investment
error_signatures.example: Says good service has no effect on profit

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Excellent service brings repeat business, good word-of-mouth and a strong reputation — it drives profit. Poor service loses customers and damages the brand.
